# Vendor integration and verification

Verified against live official documentation on 2026-09-22 using the explicitly invoked [TypeSafe skill](../../SKILL.md) and OpenAI Docs skill. No authenticated inference request was made; tests inject mocked HTTP responses and credentials.

- [TypeSafe HTTP API](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api.md), [Choice](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/choice.md), [Noul](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/noul.md), [state](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/state.md), and the [hierarchical-classification cookbook](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/hierarchical_classification.md): a request contains named state and keyed questions; one Choice supplies relative probabilities/certainty and independent Nouls supply absolute yes probabilities. The cookbook's hierarchical search is not used: this design sends all defined types together. Question IDs are identifiers, so each question explicitly references the state fields and contains the full type definition. The versioned model remains jev-1.13.0.
- [Responses create](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/cli/resources/responses/methods/create), [structured outputs](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs), [Terra](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-terra), and [Luna](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-luna): Responses uses strict text.format JSON schema; explicit max_output_tokens, store=false and truncation=disabled are included.

`requests.ts` exports immutable request builders, response decoders and `verifyModelPolicy`. `FrozenVendorRequest` includes the immutable modelPolicy as well as body bytes. Per the owner's explicit exception to the original design, approved reader aliases gpt-6-sol and historical gpt-5.6-terra, plus recovery aliases gpt-6-luna and historical gpt-5.6-luna, can accept their exact bare name or a same-family dated snapshot. Approval is role-specific; GPT-6 Luna is approved for production heading recovery; it is not a reader fallback. Other families fail. The actual returned model is preserved in raw records, normalized results and call logs. Existing strict normalized validators remain unchanged: the adapter checks the authorized family first, then validates against that verified actual ID.

Since 6 October 2026 (DECISIONS 132) the reader may also be a dated `gpt-5.4-YYYY-MM-DD` snapshot and recovery a dated `gpt-5.4-nano-YYYY-MM-DD` snapshot, both only under `versioned`: the returned `model` must equal the pin exactly, with no family or snapshot tolerance, and a bare `gpt-5.4`/`gpt-5.4-nano` is refused. The owner pack pins `gpt-5.4-2026-03-05` and `gpt-5.4-nano-2026-03-17`. The permitted families per role live in one table, `MODEL_FAMILIES` in core/config/project.ts, used by both the pack validator and `validPin` here.

Since 10 October 2026 (DECISIONS 155) `gpt-5.4`, `gpt-5.4-mini` (reader) and `gpt-5.4-nano` (recovery) are also accepted by name under `owner_approved_undated` (family `pins: 'dated-or-undated'`); the dated snapshots stay accepted under `versioned` for frozen packs. A reply to a named OpenAI request must report the family itself or one dated snapshot of it, byte-exact, or it is drift (`E_TERRA_PIN_DRIFT` / `E_LUNA_PIN_DRIFT`); a reply reporting none halts (`E_MODEL_IDENTITY_MISSING`). The run freezes the reported string and halts on a different one later in the run, as for the experimental readers. Undated is not experimental: these readers keep the pack's effort and output cap, may be the menu default, and take no `expectedModel`. The owner and practice packs request all three by name.

`executeVendor(request, policy, dependencies, decode)` invokes only injected fetch. Dependencies supply persistent guard checks (live-call gate, kill switch and budget), secret lookup, immutable R2 persistence, D1 call/usage rows, durable per-vendor failure counters, clock, unique attempt IDs and sleep. The integration must bound fetch timeouts, persist all failure events and prevent Workflow retries from restarting this whole bounded loop. Map reader/recovery circuit outcomes to their shared vendor.

Raw response body and metadata are persisted before JSON parsing; failures to persist or log halt. Tokens and returned model are logged without credentials. Missing usage on a valid successful JSON response halts because live spend cannot be omitted silently. Network failures record a typed fact, with no potentially sensitive exception text. Guard runs before every attempt and again after response logging. Any returned model outside policy halts even on retryable HTTP errors. Three transport attempts are permitted; only the reader gets one identical schema retry, with at most six requests overall. Recovery/ confidence accept one schema attempt. Every attempt gets a new artifact key. Retry-after takes precedence over the capped exponential backoff, including HTTP dates; malformed headers fail visibly. The adapter never edits prompts, request bytes, evidence or outputs during retries.

Outline recovery output still requires `verifyRecoveredHeadings`; the model only locates lines and no recovered heading is accepted without local exact-text verification.

## Experimental readers: Workers AI and DeepSeek (DECISIONS 136)

Since 6 October 2026 a pack's reader menu (`readerModels`) may also offer two non-OpenAI readers. They use the same builder, prompt, schema, validator and evidence checks as the OpenAI reader; heading recovery stays on OpenAI.

- **Qwen 3.8 27B on Cloudflare Workers AI** (`@cf/qwen/qwen3.8-27b`). Sent through the Worker's `AI` binding (`core/server/workers-ai.ts`) with `returnRawResponse: true` and no AI Gateway option, never over fetch; a frozen request names the marker `WORKERS_AI_BINDING` as its endpoint. The body is a chat completion with `response_format.json_schema` (no strict flag, because Cloudflare does not guarantee schema adherence; the validator decides), `max_completion_tokens` and `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking: false`. Usage arrives as `prompt_tokens` and `completion_tokens` and is priced by `chatUsageCost` (core/cost/README.md). Workers AI's published refusal "JSON Mode couldn't be met" takes the one identical schema retry, then fails the document. The binding is the credential; without it Health blocks this reader only.
- **DeepSeek Flash** (`deepseek-flash`). Sent to DeepSeek's Responses API (`https://api.deepseek.com/responses`), the one DeepSeek format that documents `json_schema`, with `reasoning.effort: "none"` and `max_output_tokens`. No store, truncation, cache option or strict flag is sent, because DeepSeek ignores unsupported fields silently. The key `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` is bound only in the owner configuration; a 402 (insufficient balance) is a blocker (`E_VENDOR_BALANCE`). `model-list.ts` reads `GET https://api.deepseek.com/models` once, on a DeepSeek run's first Start (`core/server/reader-version.ts`), stores the raw reply and records the version behind `deepseek-flash`; it never refuses a run.
- **Pin policy `owner_approved_undated`.** Neither id has a dated form. `verifyModelPolicy` accepts a non-empty reported model string for such a pin and refuses a reply that reports none (`E_MODEL_IDENTITY_MISSING`). The run freezes the first string and halts on any other (`core/server/model-identity.ts`); an option's recorded `expectedModel`, when set, must match every reply (`E_MODEL_PROVIDER_CHANGED`). A reply that still reports thinking halts the run (`E_READER_THINKING`).
- **Output cap.** Both use the per-category cap `per-category-v1` (2,048 + 320 per category, at most 16,384), frozen with the run. An answer that reaches it is never read: after the one identical retry the document fails with `E_READER_OUTPUT_LIMIT`.
- **Daily reservations.** OpenAI requests are counted exactly with `POST /v1/responses/input_tokens` before they are sent. Neither Workers AI nor DeepSeek documents a count endpoint, so `input-token-count.ts` reserves the request's UTF-8 byte length as its input bound, plus the full output cap.
- **Pretend vendors.** `fake-vendors.ts` answers both readers and DeepSeek's model list; the pretend build refuses every credential binding, the AI binding included.

## Batch mode (retired)

Batch mode was retired on 26 September 2026 (owner decision, 25 September 2026): `batch.ts`, `batch-closure.ts`, the Batch request builders in `requests.ts` and the server's `batch-runner.ts` were deleted. The Batch tables stay in the schema as history. The guards that refused or held back runs created in that mode were removed on 5 October 2026, because no installation this code runs on holds one (the cutover is a clean replacement).

## Cache controls

The request follows the pack's recorded `settings.promptCachePolicy` (core/cost/README.md, "Prompt-cache policies"); the builders take it as `cachePolicy` and refuse (`E_MODEL_POLICY`) a policy the pinned model's family does not support. Under `automatic-cache-priced-v1` (gpt-5.4 and gpt-5.4-nano, owner pack since 6 October 2026) the request carries no `prompt_cache_options` at all, because OpenAI documents that option for GPT-5.6 and later only; otherwise the request is byte-identical, and the model's automatic caching is priced from the usage it reports. The rest of this section describes `explicit-no-cache-v1`, which a stored pack without the setting recorded.

Reader/recovery under `explicit-no-cache-v1` set prompt_cache_options.mode=explicit and no prompt_cache_breakpoint markers. Official Responses documentation says this removes the implicit cache breakpoint, and explicit-only cache lookup checks only explicit breakpoints. Thus these single-turn requests select no cached prefix. This transport option does not change model-visible content. The no-cache policy was chosen during the owner-authorized spending review on 2026-09-22 to avoid the GPT-5.6 cache-write premium and discount accounting ambiguity. `actualUsageCost` requires explicit zero read/write cache counters; unexpected cached usage blocks accounting rather than silently treating it at ordinary rates. See the cost README for official source links and integration requirements.

## Approved reader promotion (2026-09-23)

The owner approved GPT-6 Sol for new runs after five paired documents produced identical reader yes-sets and decision-rule replays with 13.3% lower selected-completion cost; this small provisional comparison establishes no general quality advantage. Existing frozen Terra run packs remain valid. Reader prompt, low effort, 16,384 output cap, full text, exact evidence checks and deterministic decision rules are unchanged. Recovery remains GPT-5.6 Luna.

Reverified the official [GPT-6 Sol model page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6-sol) on 2026-09-23: Responses and structured outputs, low effort, 1,050,000 context, standard USD2 input/USD10 output per million tokens, and the existing above-272,000-token 2x input/1.5x output tier. Account throughput remains explicitly unknown in the packs.
